analysis: This batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/provider-fast-reconnect.md lines 1-5, docs/architecture/components/provider.md head lines 3, 40 and 119-144, and docs/provider/cli-reference.md head lines 1968-1971. The docs describe a new CoordinatorReconnectPolicy. A session open for 60s or more after its register frame resets the backoff. A coordinator-side close with code 1012 draws a 0-1s wait and does not grow the backoff. Other ends keep ExponentialBackoff(1,30). The close code is parsed from the first two payload bytes (sentCloseCode) when Network.framework reports noStatusReceived. The docs state that registration, attestation, the fresh per-socket nonce, resume-state clearing and cancellation of the old connection's requests are unchanged. That is consistent with TB-002, TB-011 and T-053. No Swift source for CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, CoordinatorClientState.swift or CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift was supplied, so these claims are unverified. Integration questions: (1) Is the 1012 close code taken only from frames received on the authenticated TLS coordinator socket? A network attacker cannot inject frames, but a malicious or compromised endpoint could force rapid reconnects. Such reconnects are bounded at about 1/s and the provider is the client, so availability impact on the provider (A-018) seems low. A related question is whether the coordinator can absorb a synchronized fleet reconnect within 0-1s after a restart (thundering herd, platform-owned). (2) The close-payload parsing should bounds-check payloads shorter than 2 bytes. (3) Is the stable-session timer started only after a successful register? The docs say it counts from the register frame; confirm it is not counted from the TCP connect. (4) Confirm that a faster reconnect does not let late App Attest results or stale grants survive across transports. The docs say AppAttestShadowReply remains bound to the original NWConnection (T-053). Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a security regression, so there are no findings; the source should be reviewed in its own batch.
